     Introduction
      The AZADEGAN Oilfield is Located in Khuzestan Province and is Approximately
Located 80 Kilometers West of Ahwaz City, Near to Iran-Iraq Border. It is in The Northwest
of The YADAVARAN Field and in The West of JUFEYR Field. The Average Monthly
Temperature is 45ºc in summer, and Highest Temperature is 52ºc. The Lowest Temperature is
-4.4ºc in winter. Maximum Rainfall is 78 mm in February, Winter Season.
      The Field is in Flooding Plain Area with Convenient Road Network which Extends to
Ahwaz. Most of The Oil Fields in The Region are Located in The Foothill Zone Zagros Folded
Zone of the NW-SE Trending Zagros Mountain Range, and Have Similar Trends to The Zagros
Mountain Range Elongated Anticline Structure.
       This Document Covers the Drilling of Gadvan Producer Well in South Azadegan
Oilfield, Iran. Well G-04 Shall Be Considered to Produce from the Gadvan Reservoir. Plan is
to KOP 3585m. Commence Directional Drilling 8-1/2” Hole to 7” Liner Setting Depth at 3934
M. Then 7” Liner will be Run and Cemented and Continue Operation with Directional drilling
6 1/8” Hole Section about 350 m horizontally in Gadvan 5C Formation to 4284 M. The 4-1/2”
Slotted Liner will be run to TD & Run Standard Completion String, N/Up Well Head and
Complete Well.

    S373 Highly Deviated Well on Pad-48 Objectives
   As The Previous Exploration/Delineation Drilling in AZADEGAN Oil Field has Proved
Presence of a Very Prolific Hydrocarbon Bearing Sedimentary Column, Particularly within the
Cretaceous Sequences.
G-04 Gadvan producer well is planned to be drilled in Pad-26 which is located in the North part
of South Azadegan oil field in Area-I.
Far away from Gadvan OWC and achieve the better reservoir quality, this well is planned as
Horizontal well with Azimuth of 40 degree.
Figure 1 shows the position of Pad-26 on the underground contour map on top of Gadvan.
The Horizontal well (G-04) will be drilled down to Gadvan Reservoir and subsequently will be
completed as a Gadvan reservoir oil producer.

    Pore and Fracture Press Prediction

       Since the Formation Pressure of Gachsaran Formation is Different between North Area
and South Near and Decreases Greatly and Complete Loss Took Place at all Four Existing
Wells in South Area, the Oilfield is divided into three Areas.
      Area I (North of AZN-10): Area I Located in North of Line1(Y-Coordinate: 3452051),
in this Area, Gachsaran Formation is Characterized with Abnormal High Pressure. For No
Wells have ever been Drilled in the Area between Line1 (Y-Coordinate: 3452051) and Line 3
(Y-Coordinate: 3457993), This Area Exists Greater Uncertainties and is Delimited to the Area
I Temporarily.
      Area II (Between AZN-10 and AZN-11): Area II Located between Line1 (Ycoordinate:
3452051) and Line 2 (Y-Coordinate: 3443549), in this Area, the Formation of Gachsaran
Formation Decreases Greatly.
      Area III (South of AZN-11): Area III Located the South of Line 2 (Y-Coordinate:
3443549), in this Area, the Formation of Gachsaran Formation Decreases Greatly and all
Existing Wells Occurred Complete Loss at Pabdeh Formation.
      The Area Division shall be Adjusted According to Further Actual Drilling Operation,
and Quantity of Wells in Different Areas could be also Adjusted Accordingly.

    Program Outline
          It is planned to drill and complete a Gadvan Horizontal well.
     26" Hole section:
      The 26” Hole Section will be Drilled 154 M through Aghajari Formation. Aghajari
Formation Consists of A Marl, Sand-Shale. For Drilling This Section 67-69 pcf Pre-Hydrated
Bentonite Mud will be used for Hole Cleaning. Also PHB Pill Will Be Used to Clean the Hole
and Since Bentonite has the Best Cake around the Well Bore, It will make a Good Cake for
Hole Stability. According to Previous Wells in this Field, this Section is almost Problem Free.
The 20" Casing will be set at ±150 M and it will be cemented in One Stage with Stinger (Exact
CMT Program will be issued in Due Time). N/U 20-3/4" 3k C.H.H & 21 1/4" 2K Annular
BOP and Single Rams.

      17-1/2" Hole section:
       This Section will be drilled from ±154 M to ±1400 M through Aghajari Formation.
According to offset Wells tight spots, Hard Back Ream, W&R while RIH and Bit Balling Up
in surface was recorded. For Drilling This Section 70-80 Pcf Kcl/Nacl Polymer Mud will be
Used. Also PHB Pill will be used to clean the Hole. CDR/GR log will be run in open hole. 13
3/8" Casing Shoe will Be Set at ±1400 M about 55m below the Top of Gachsaran to Case off
Full Soft Unconsolidated Formation of Lower Aghajari and Drill the next Hole Section with
different Mud Density. It will be cemented in One Stage (Lead & Tail - Exact CMT Program
will be issued in Due Time). N/Up C.H.S 20-3/4" 3k x 13-5/8” 5K. N/U 13-5/8" 10K BOP’s
Stack (13 5/8" 5K Annular Preventer + 13 5/8" 10K Double Rams + 13 5/8" 10K Single).

     12 ¼" Hole Section:
       This Section will be drilled from ±1400 to ±1780 M through Gachsaran. For Drilling
this Section the 115-125 Pcf KCl Polymer Mud can be used. The Risks of Drilling this Section
is Heavy MW & High pressure formation, Low ROP, Tight Hole and Stuck Pipe Based on
Offset Wells. CDR/GR Log Will Be Run in Open Hole. 9 5/8" Casing Shoe will be set at ±1780
M at the 5m above Top of Asmari to Isolate High Pressure Formation for Drilling to Next
Section to TD with low Mud Weight. It will be cemented in One Stage (Lead & Tail -Exact
CMT Program will be issued in Due Time). CCL/GR/CBL-VDL Will Be Run. N/U T.H.S 13
5/8" 5k x 11" 10k. N/U 13-5/8” 10K BOP’s Stack. (13 5/8" 5k Annular BOP + 13 5/8" 10k
Double Rams + 13 5/8" 10K Single).

     8 ½” Hole Section (Vertical and Directional):
       This Section will be drilled from ±1780 to 3585 M (KOP) & Cont’ drlg to 3934M (7”
Liner Setting Depth) will be drilled as Directionally through Dariyan & Gadvan Formations.
Which Consist of Sandstone & lime stone, marl & shale. MWD/LWD with GR Should be used
in Directional Drilling as Survey & Resistivity Tools from KOP to Hole Section TD. The CDR
log should run on wireline. The Full suite log should be run with TLC method. 75-81 Pcf Kcl
Polymer Mud Will Be Used For Drilling This Section. Then 7” Liner will be run ±3934M and
Cemented in One Stage (Exact CMT Program will be issued in Due Time). CCL/GR/CBL-
VDL Will Be Run after Perform 7” Cementing Job.

     6 1/8" Hole Section (Directional):
       This Section will be Drilled from ±3934 M MD to ±4284 M MD in Gadvan Formation
Zone-5C As Horizontal. 81-82 Pcf Kcl Polymer Mud will Be Used for Drilling this Section.
The Risks of Drilling This Section is Drilling Fluid Loss, Tight Hole and Stuck Pipe Based on
Offset Wells. MWD/LWD/GR will be used in Horizontal open Hole. Run a full suite log as
TLC method. 4-1/2” Slotted Liner will be run to ±4284 mMD and Hang Off. Displace hole
with completion fluid. Then the Well will be completed as Gadvan Producer well.

    If well is not completed the temporary abandon program will be issued at due
      time by contractor

    Formation Description
    A brief description of the stratigraphic units expected to be drilled in South Azadegan
typical well has been presented in the following breakdown.

    Recent/Aghajari Formation
      The Aghajari Formation consists of a repetition of brown to grey calcareous Sandstones,
chert debris and gypsum-veined red marl. A fauna of brackish to freshwater was observed,
together with more marine fauna.

   Gachsaran Formation
      The Gachsaran Formation with a thickness ranges from 400 m to 600 m, thicken towards
the north. Deposition of the Gachsaran Formation is cyclic. The cycle began with a deposition
of shallow-water marine carbonates, and then it was overlain by a thick evaporitic phase. The
evaporites were capped by red to variegated marl, which represented the end of cycle.

   Asmari Formation
      The Asmari Formation in Azadegan Field developed a massive sandstone interval, with
a few thin argillaceous layers in the upper sections. Sands are clear, fine to medium-sorted, and
poorly consolidated. On the other hand, the lower sections consist of intercalation of sandy,
chalky, slightly dolomitic high-energy limestone with sands layers.

   Pabdeh Formation
      Pabdeh Formation is divided into two parts in the Azadegan field. The upper part is
made of grey to dark-brown argillaceous limestones and marls. Planktonic fauna dates that this
part. was deposited in Oligocene. The lower part  is composed of dark-brown, slightly
argillaceous limestone. Pelagic fauna, mostly Globigerina and Globorotalia, indicates that this
part was formed during late Paleocene to late Eocene in age. It seems that no early Paleocene
Formation exists in the Azadegan area.

   Gurpi Formation
      The Gurpi Formation in the Azadegan Field consists of grey to dark-brownish, slightly
argillaceous micritic limestone with Maestrichtian to Campanian aged fauna. At Well AZN-1,
about 50 meters of chalky limestones were encountered in the middle of the Gurpi formation,
which contains abundant fragments of rudists, bryozoa, corals, and Orbitoides.

    Ilam Formation
       In the Azadegan Field, the Ilam Formation consists of grey micritic limestone, often
argillaceous, rarely pyritic, limestones. Microfauna, mostly pelagic, including rotalids and
oligostegina assemblage, a few algae, bryozoa, and rudist fragments exist.

 GEOLOGICAL INFORMATION                                     Page 28 of 177

                     Well : AZNS-118 (G04)

         Page 29 of 177                Doc. No.: AZD6-EN-WP-020-1                     Rev: 1

    Laffan Formation
      The Laffan Formation developed a thin greenish-grey pyritic shale layer, capping the
Sarvak Formation. It was encountered in the Azadegan wells and only ostracods were found.
It is a cap rock for the upper part of the Sarvak reservoir.

   Sarvak Formation
      The Sarvak Formation developed a carbonate unit which was gradually overlying the
Kazhdumi Formation, and it was abruptly terminated by an erosion phase and covered by
various late Cretaceous sediments. A Typical geological section of the Sarvak Formation in
Azadegan reveals that dark grey fine grained nodulary argillaceous limestone interbedded with
thin marls in the bottom, and graded upward into a white-to-buff massive chalky limestone with
siliceous nodules; it was developed a very massive tan-to-brown limestone containing abundant
rudist debris in the middle part; the upper part is made up of rubbly limestone with red staining
and leached zones of breccia and the top of Sarvak Formation is very ferruginous

   Kazhdumi Formation
       In the Azadegan Field, the upper part of the Kazhdumi Formation is made up of dark -
grey to dark-brown marls, the middle part developed light-grey, micritic to chalky limestone,
the low part, is around40-60m in thickness clean channel sands interbeded argillaceous sands
with streaks of shale.

   Gadvan Formation
       In the Gadvan Formation, a variety of lithological rock types such as carbonates, rich
organic shales and sandstones were deposited in various environments. The lower part of the
Gadvan Formation is composed of low-energy, but not very deep, micritic, often argillaceous
limestone with echinoids and algal fragments. Two sandstone units were defined in the Gadvan
Formation lateral changes and especially discontinuity of the sandstone layers which are onsist
of fine clastics (shales and siltstones) may be expected

    E.1.2. Sequence of Operation
   Make up 26” BHA as per BHA design. Tag formation at ±14m.
     Drill ahead formation down to 154M (20” casing point in Aghajari formation) using hi-
      vis bentonite pill. Pay enough attention to drill straight hole.
     Note: TD should be adjusted to have Min 2m of rat hole below casing shoe.
-    The exact TD will be determined based on casing tally.
-    Run Inclinometer each 50m to evaluate the verticality of the hole.
-    Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable
      condition.
-    Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.
-    Enough Mud Material, LCM and Cement Should be Available before spud the rig to use
      in case of needing.
-    1 Set pump truck should be available on well site before start drilling.
-   Mud Logging unit should be available from rig spud.
-    At TD, Circulate and clean the hole. Take Survey, POOH to surface. Check Bit.

    Sequence of Operation

────────────────────────────────────────────
                        Drilling Program
                     Well : AZNS-118 (G04)
                        Type : IGH

         Page 65 of 177                Doc. No.: AZD6-EN-WP-020-1                     Rev: 1

    Perform a reamer trip due to conditioning the hole prior to run casing. If observe any
      indication of drag, run back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure that the hole
      condition is good.
    Perform Safety meeting.
   R/U casing running equipment.
   Run ±150m (Approx. 15 Jts) 20", 94 ppf, K-55, BTC casing with duplex shoe to bottom
      as per casing program. Casing shoe should be adjusted to have 1m of rat hole and enough
      stick up (1 m on rig floor). Fill casing by non LCM fresh mud.
     Note: Take care when running casing not to set down excessive weight if tight hole or
      ledges are encountered.
   Run stinger on DP’s using the “C” Plate & 5” x 20” centralizer. Sting in. M/U & test
     cementing lines. Circulate for one casing annulus volume. While circulating, check the
    DPs annulus for any return. Use all DPs weight on the string if observing any minor
     leakage through DPs annulus.
    Perform pilot test on cement & take sample from cement solution
    Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth will
     be done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl. Short Displace). Monitor for pressures.
     Record and report the final pressure, Sting out. Check the float. POOH one stand,
      Circulate to flush/clean drill pipe.
     After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor & flush it.
   POOH to surface. L/D stinger.
    Keep the casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check for casing
      to be center inside conductor pipe.
       Note: Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to
            perform top-up jobs.
-      If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to fill the annulus.
     Use same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry. Ensure the availability of adequate
     X-over for connecting line pipe to cement line. The cement should be accelerated with
     max. (2%) Calcium Chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement
      to get hard.
    Check Cement by slack off weight.
    Cut conductor pipe. Rough cut landing joint and L/D C.P. and L.J. Dress and bevel 20”
      suitable to install and to weld casing head spool.
     Install and weld casing head housing 20-3/4” – 3000 psi on casing and pressure test the
      sealing of welded casing. (Limit pressure to 400 psi a maximum of 80% of the collapse
     strength of the casing). Outlets must be aligning with cellar stairs.
     Note:
-    Check the 20 3/4” wear bushing, 20 3/4” Plug Tester and 13-3/8” Casing Slip and seal
     assembly in CHH before installing CHH (on Surface).
      If cellar is standard the distance between its top flange and ground level must be 1.73m.

       R/U & run fullsuite wireline/TLC log.
       L/D logging tools.
       RIH as condition trip prior to run 7” liner.
        Check wiper plug in LDC for Leakage. Check ball size in LDC.
        Perform Function test, flow through & hold test for float shoe & float collar in start of
         running Liner.
       Run 7” Liner as per Program and Hang (1720-3934 M). 7”, 29 lb/ft, L80(1), Gas Tight
         Conn. , Float Shoe should be set 0.5 meters off bottom.
        Note :
     -     Fill string w/ fresh mud (NO LCM) while RIH.
     -     7”, 29 lb/ft, L80(1), Gas Tight Conn. Float Collar should be installed one joint above
          the shoe & LDC should be installed one joint above Float Collar.
     -   Bow Centralizer every 3 joints, 7” rigid centralizers on third and fourth joints from top.
     -    7” Hyd. Liner Hanger Must Be Suitable inside 9-5/8” CSG 47# with top packer.

     7” Liner running procedure:
    After making up the shoe track, lower through rotary table and check that the floats are
      holding. Fill up with mud and pick up to check float functionality. Circulate for 10 min.
   Run liner at controlled speed to minimize pressure surges (approx. 12 joints/hr). Check
      returns constantly.
     Fill up liner completely every 10 joints run.
   When the required numbers of liner joints have been made up, make up the liner hanger
     without Top Packer, running tool as per liner hanger engineer’s instructions.
     Circulate 120% of the liner capacity. (Record Liner weight)
   Run the liner with 5” DP to 9-5/8” CSG, Mud Circulation as 120% of String Cap to
     check String, Liner hanger engineer should be on rig floor while running liner into open
      hole.
    Use Torque measuring System (TMS) for makeup casing, observe torque graph.
   NOTE : Check the loss while RIH if need Decrease the Speed of the RIH.
   SLM & drift the drill pipe while RIH the liner.
    Continue Run to Bottom hole, Tag Bottom, 0.5 m Move Up string, Mud Circulation as
    150% of String Cap.
   M/U combination plug dropping head to the last joint. Use pup joint, if necessary.
    The hanger will be set 64 m above the 9-5/8” Shoe.
    Try to avoid setting hanger on casing coupling. Use 9 5/8” casing Tally. Set the Hanger
      as per hanger engineer procedure. Ensure that the running tool is free of the liner (work
      string 0.5m up and down – record loss of weight as the hanger sets) before starting to
     cement.
    Perform Pilot test on cement slurry, take sample from cement solution for testing
    Cement 7" liner as per cementing program.
    Displace the cement with the cementing pump to the liner wiper plug. Shear out liner
     wiper plug (Record the volume pumped and shearing pressure). Displace combined
     wiper plugs to latch down collar.
   Bump the plug with max. 3000 psi (Record and report final displacement pressure prior
      to bump the plug). If there is no bump, do not displace more than 25% of the shoe-track
     volume. Displace with Cementing Pump and record cement losses.
    Hold bumping pressure for 5 minutes. If the plugs bumped.
      If plugs bumped, pressure up and test liner to 3000 psi for 15 minutes.
    Bleed off pressure slowly and check for back-flow.
    P/U setting tool for two meters , check for U tube f/ DP & N/D Cementing Head
    While Cementing Mud Engineer must have level of Mud Tanks and announce any Loss
      or return.
   POH to Surface While Lay Down Excess 6-1/2"DCs and 5" DPs on Floor.

   RIH with 8-1/2” R.Bit to 7” Liner Lap while D/O Hard Cement above it (if any) , Tag
    Top of Liner, CBU
    Perform Positive test with 2000psi/15min.

      out cement  , D/O Plugs, LDC and CMT to maximum 7m above 7”. float Shoe (Touch
     hard cement) .
    Perform CIT with 3000psi/15min.

-      If there is not any Cement Above 7" L.Lap Dry test should be performed and If Hard
     cement was touched the decision will be made. If Needed to Perform 7” L.Lap Dry
      Test, the Program will be Issued in due Time.
      If decided to Perform Dry test for top of Liner, with 2000psi differential pressure
      (underbalance). Report the result in DDR.

      out 7” shoe & collar.

    E.5.2. Sequence of Operation
   Make up 6-1/8” Roller Cone Bit w/ New BHA (Junk Sub Included), RIH to Top of CMT
   & D/O CMT to 7”. Float collar (Top Plug).
     Drill out plugs, float collar and cement to 2m above shoe. (* After drill to 7m above LDC,
     Perform Casing Pressure test if bumping not observed) Balance Mud in hole with 81 Pcf
    KCL Mud and Obs. the Well Several Times, Drill out Remained Cement and 7”. Float
     shoe and Cement of rat hole & 1m Below Shoe, observe well for 1 Hrs for any Loss or
      flow. (Watch carefully for any indication of abnormal torque, since there might be the
      risk of shoe back off. In case, report immediately.)
      If the well is static drill ahead to 2M below shoe, work on junk sub, observe well. C.B.U.

                                     , L/D J.Sub.   POOH to surface,

  1.  Fill the tanks with the required volume of Drill water.
     Note: Drill water should be tested before mixing and if its hardness is more than 400mg/l, it
 should    be treated.

  2. Add 0.5-0.7 lb/bbl of CAUSTIC SODA to prepare brine to pH 10.5.
  3. Add 0.7-1 lb/bbl of SODA ASH to control hardness in acceptable range below 400mg/lit
     (To achieve better Ca++ settling, pH have to be kept above 10.5).

  4. Add 20-30 lb/bbl of Bentonite and allow hydrating for as long as possible. Processing with a
     shearing device will improve yield.
  5. Add 0.5-1 lb/bbl LIME to system to adjust pH.

G.1.2.    Interval Key Issues
          Loss Zone: There is a possibility of complete loss in this interval with No Return
          mud, so LCM pill should be prepared before drilling of this section as contingency.

          Hole Cleaning: Hole cleaning problems could be avoided by proper use of viscosifiers,
               e.g. BENTO-GEL API.

G.1.3.    Engineering Outline & System Maintenance

       To achieve better Ca++ settling, pH have to be kept above 10
       The Plastic Viscosity value should be minimized by optimum usage of the solids control
      equipment and by dilution with pre-mix, where applicable, to generate new volume and / or
      reduce mud rheology. Shaker Screen Size should be selected 86 Mesh API.

       Yield point should be kept high (the program range) to reduce the annular flow rates required
      and gel value are required to reach to maximum hole cleaning.

        available while drilling.

  Drilling Fluids Properties

  To solve problems associated with this interval and increase the ROP, CLAY-BOND FLUID SYSTEM
  has been designed to drill the formation and inhibit clay and marl problems in this section.
  CLAY-BOND L has also been successfully used to drill clay interbeds in both saline and non-saline
   systems. It is very important to determine MBT of mud during drilling and keep it in the program range.
   Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens,
   start with 68 pcf MW and increase every 100 meter 1 pcf using salts up to 75 pcf and then BARA-
 WATE API up to 78 pcf.
  Note: to serve a better hole cleaning, consider the following procedure prior to each trip and
   circulation:
        Pump polymeric Hi-Vis pill having funnel viscosity of 70 to 85 using 1.5-2 lb of BIO-XCD
        and 1.5-2 lb PAC UHV.

     1-  Fill the tanks with 100 bbl of Drill water.
     2- Add 65-70 lb/bbl of SODIUM CHLORIDE AC (NaCl).
     3- Add 0.5-1 lb/bbl of CAUSTIC SODA to adjust pH around 10-11.
     4- Add 2%vol ROP ENHANCER (2 Drum/100 bbl)
     5- When ROP is low pump this pill or pump 50bbl of this pill every 100m.

G.2.2. Interval Key Issues
      Loss Zone: There is a possibility of complete loss in this interval with No Return mud, so
     LCM pill should be prepared before drilling this section as contingency.
       Bit Balling: Due to the clay and marl characteristic of the formation, bit balling is one of the
       main problems. It is required to use KCL R-UPG and CLAY-BOND L according to the above
       mentioned to provide cutting encapsulation during drilling.
      Clay & Marl Inhibition: Tight hole might be experienced in this interval due to existence of
        clay & marl in the formation. Good inhibition will be helpful to provide stable hole condition.
       Salt Water Flow:  There is a possibility of salt water flow. Therefore close monitoring is
        required to maintain Ca++ and pH level.

G.2.3. Engineering Outline & System Maintenance

      Mud weight to be kept between 68 and 78 pcf unless hole dictates, salts and BARA-WATE
      API will be used to rise the mud weight. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE
       and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens (150/ 200 mesh size) if possible.
       Dump and dilution is one of the best ways to keep the MW on the guideline especially with
         clean mud systems. Running all solids equipment and dump and dilution would be the
         best way to control the MW (after drilling each stand, 25 bbl can be dumped from
          sandtrap).
       Rheological properties of the mud should be monitored to ensure maximum hole cleaning.
       Contamination with cement will increase the rheological properties of the mud especially the
          yield point. Therefore, prior to cement, YP should be reduced to the minimum level if
           practical.

G.2.4. Lesson Learned and Recommendation
 These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be
 useful to drill this well if used.
       It is very important to determine MBT of mud during drilling and keep it in the program range.
      Running all solids equipment and dump and dilution would be the best way to control the
     MW.
      Due to undesirable hole condition and hard casing running, regular wash and ream should be
       performed on each drilled stand.
       Increasing mud weight smoothly, improve hole condition in previous well.
      Regarding high ROP, pre-treatment is a critical item while drilling this section.

 G.3.1. Drilling Fluids Formulation
  To drill this section a Salt Saturated Polymer Mud with 115-125 pcf would be used. Salt would be
   used up to the saturation level (75 pcf) to prohibit the thin inter bedded layers of Salt in member 7 &
  2 from being washed and also will act as a strong shale inhibitor in the system and maintain MW as
   per pore pressure curve dictates in the drilling program using BARA-WATE API.
  Mud Weight should be increased 1 pcf every 30m up to 125 pcf, more than 125 pcf should be done
   with company man permission.
  Rheology of the system would be raised by using BIO-XCD (Optional).
  AMYLOSE LV, a modified starch would be used as a filtration control agent in this section. The
  main concern in this section is the effect of the formation water on the mud properties. If any problem
   rises during the drilling, AMYLOSE LV should be replaced with the PAC ULV at the concentration
   between 1-1.5 lb/bbl.

G.3.2. Interval Key Issues

       Salt Water Flow: Gachsaran formation has the potential of salt water flow. The hardness of
        this water is between 35000-53000 mg/l, so any increase in the hardness of mud would be an
       indication of possible salt water flow. Therefore, during drilling this section, hardness of the
      system must be checked and monitored three times per day for any increase in Ca++ ions.

       Losses: In the upper part of Gachsaran a weak zone has been experienced. Layers interbedded
       in the salts in Gachsaran Members 2 & 3 can have normal pressure, and therefore a reduced
       fracture gradient compared to the salt layers. Heavy losses might be experienced in Gachsaran.
       Losses have also been seen in the first shale layer of Cap Rock, its second layer from the top,
       so it is very important not to drill deeper than approximately one meter into this Member.

       Stuck Pipe: Tight hole / stuck pipe in the 12 1/4" hole section is typically isolated to the
      Shales/Clay stones and salt beds. The stuck in Shales and clay stones as far as the MW is
       adjusted correctly and FL is tight and the salinity is up to saturation is not a matter of concern.

G.3.3. Engineering Outline & System Maintenance

  Mud Weight
 In the initial mixing, salt would be the first weighting agent up to 75 pcf, then BARA WATE API
 will be used to reach to 125 pcf as hole conditions dictate. Controlling the mud weight meanwhile
 drilling would be done by running all SCE and dump and dilution. Pore pressure is expected to be
 marginally above the normal pressure in the Jurassic / Upper Triassic.
 Mud weight selection is critical in this interval. In some offset wells, excessive losses may occur in
 the Gachsaran member 7 when the mud weight is higher than the optimum. On the other hand, in
 some offset wells, water flow could be encountered when the mud weight is allowed to fall down
 below optimum MW.

────────────────────────────────────────────
                           Drilling Program
                        Well : AZNS-118 (G04)

 It is important to drill this section with the mud weight being kept as per the guide line, also by
 running all solids control equipments and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens; it is possible
 to minimize the ECD and the potential for induced losses.

   Shale Inhibition
 Salt would be used for shale inhibition to combat the Gachsaran Marl/Shale’s. However, the very
 tight FL would be the other shale inhibition property of the system. Controlling the salinity up to
 saturation is vital to drill into Gachsaran formation against troublesome Shales/Marls.

   Rheological Properties
 PV is always to be kept as low as possible by reducing the drilled solids concentrations of mud using
 the proper installation of the solids control equipment so that the hydraulics is optimized.
 High gel values are required to support the high quantity of weighting agents while tripping, making
 connections and during survey times. PV should be kept in the range mentioned in the drilling fluid
 program.

  A thin salt bed in Gachsaran member 2 is a red flag for Geologist that means reaching to cap rock
 is imminent, salinity below the saturation will cause the salt samples to be dissolved in the system
 resulting in no salt sample over the shakers.

G.3.4. Lesson Learned and Recommendation
 These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be
 useful to drill this well if used.
      Due to undesirable hole condition while tripping and casing running, performing wash and
       ream on each drilled stand is the best way to have good hole condition.
       Availability and running decenter centrifuge to remove LGS in this section is critical.
       It is important to drill this section with the mud weight being kept as per the guide line. Also
       by running all solids control equipment and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens; it
          is possible to minimize the ECD and the potential for induced losses.
     A low as PV is required in this section to eliminate Mud Gel Up by suitable SCE layout.

G.4.2. Interval Key Issues

  Swab possibility
 Special care must be taken when the BHA is inside the previous casing. In contrary to popular
 belief, pressure does travel easily in drilling fluids, so tripping speed must be controlled to avoid
 swabbing.

  Stuck Pipe
 The combination of different size of CARBO-WATE incorporated into the mud will form a thin and
 slick filter cake in borehole and prevent the risk of stuck pipe.

   Drilling Issues
 When drilling through fractured lime stones, swabbing of hydrocarbons can be experienced. Influx
 due to overpressure vs. influx due to swabbing must be differentiated.

   Losses
 Pressure differences between the different reservoir zones in this section can cause lost circulation
 problems. It is recommended to drill with as low as possible mud weight through the reservoir.

  H2S & CO2 Gases
 There is possibility for existence of H2S and CO2 Gases in the reservoir zones (Asmari,Pabdeh, Ilam
 and Sarvak), it is recommended to keep the pH around 9.5 to 10 and also using H2S SCAV P to
 prevent mud properties from being changed.

G.4.3. Engineering Outline & System Maintenance

  Mud Weight
 A mud weight of 75-81 pcf will be used to drill this section, a mixture of Calcium Carbonate different
 grades will be used to reduce the filter cake thickness. It is preferred to use CARBO-WATE bridging
 agent rather than the conventional Calcium Carbonate.

  Rheology
 Mud Rheology was justified to ensure maximum hole cleaning in both dynamic and static conditions.
 Using BIO-XCD/ PAC UHV would help to adjust the YP and 6/3 RPM.
 PV is always to be kept as low as possible by reducing the drilled solids concentrations of mud using
 the proper installation of the solids control equipment so that the hydraulics is optimized.
 YP is selected to be in the programmed range. High YP values are recommended to reduce the annular
 flow rates required and consequently less hole erosion.

   Shale Inhibition
 To provide maximum inhibition during drilling this section, KCL R-UPG concentration should be
 kept at 3%-5% Wt and GLYCO-DRILL and CLAY-BOND L should be added before entering to the
 shale interval.

                           Drilling Program

  pH
 During normal drilling operations, pH should be kept above a minimum of 9.0 in an attempt to
 minimize polymer degradation, to neutralize any H2S gas in the mud and to reduce the corrosion rate
 of the drill string.

  API Fluid Loss
 This hole section will be drilled using ULTRA-INHIBIT FLUID SYSTEM. It is recommended to
 maintain the fluid loss below 3 cc/30 min using FL control polymers to minimize the filter cake
 thickness.

   Reduced Dilution Rates
 GLYCO-DRILL GP improves the inhibition and stability of clays and shales and field data has shown
 that much lower dilution rates are required to maintain optimum mud properties. In some cases, the
 fluid can even be recycled to give further cost and environmental savings.
 GLYCO-DRILL GP improves filter cake quality and reduces fluid loss as the cloud point threshold is
 exceeded, the micro-emulsion formed by the now insoluble Glyco-Drill will help to reduce the HPHT
 fluid loss. This improvement in filter cake quality and the lower fluid loss will significantly reduce
 the chances of differential stickin

G.4.4. Lesson Learned and Recommendation
 These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be
 useful to drill this well if used.

      Previous Wells show rheological drop may be occurred while drilling Asmari Formation.
       Keeping YP in desired range avoids probable washout in this formation.
      Gas and oil influx have been recorded in previous wells, mud weight should be designed to
        prevent influx in Gurpi and Ilam formations.
      The combination of different size of CARBO-WATE incorporated into the mud will form a
         thin and slick filter cake in borehole and prevent the risk of stuck pipe.
      High level of inhibition is critical while drilling Pabdeh, Gurpi, Laffan and Kazhdomi
        formations. Sloughing shale has been recorded in previous wells.
      Due to the importance of drilling this section, after drilling each stand in shale and clay
         intervals the same stand should be Wash and Ream completely before connection and
        continuing drilling.
       It is recommended to maintain the fluid loss below 3 cc/30 min using the FL control polymers
         to minimize the filter cake thickness.

   Shale Inhibition
 To provide maximum inhibition during drilling this section, KCL R-UPG concentration should be
 kept at 5% Wt and GLYCO-DRILL and ASPHA SHALE NHP should be added to system.

  pH
 During normal drilling operations, pH should be kept above a minimum of 9.0 in an attempt to
 minimize polymer degradation, to neutralize any H2S gas in the mud and to reduce the corrosion rate
 of the drill string.

  API Fluid Loss
 This hole section will be drilled using SHALE-DRILL FLUID SYSTEM. It is recommended to maintain
 the fluid loss below 3 cc/30 min using FL control polymers to minimize the filter cake thickness.

                        Well : AZNS-118 (G04)
                           Type : IGH

             Page 110 of 177               Doc. No.: AZD6-EN-WP-020-1                     Rev: 1

   Reduced Dilution Rates
 GLYCO-DRILL GP improves the inhibition and stability of clays and shales and field data has shown
 that much lower dilution rates are required to maintain optimum mud properties. In some cases, the
 fluid can even be recycled to give further cost and environmental savings.

 GLYCO-DRILL GP improves filter cake quality and reduces fluid loss as the cloud point threshold is
 exceeded, the micro-emulsion formed by the now insoluble Glyco-Drill will help to reduce the HPHT
 fluid loss. This improvement in filter cake quality and the lower fluid loss will significantly reduce
 the chances of differential sticking.

G.5.4.    Lesson Learned and Recommendation
 These recommendation were prepared based on lesson learned of previous drilled wells, they can be
 useful to drill this well if used.

      Due to the importance of drilling this section, after drilling each stand in shale and clay
         intervals the same stand should be Wash and Ream completely before connection and
        continuing drilling.
      Adequate shale and clay inhibition is necessary during drilling this section.

G.6.1.  Clean up and Completion Program
 This program describes the procedure to clean up and displace the cased hole from water based mud
 brine as safely and effectively as possible prior to running the completion equipment.
 Clean working practices and good housekeeping as always are important.

 All rig pits, ditches, and lines (including gun lines) should be cleaned using solvents and detergents.  If
 it is practical, lines should be opened to check for any mud solids that might have settled in them.

 All the pits, sand traps, and under the shale shakers should be cleaned out and washed down using high
 pressure cleaning equipment. In the pit room, all gratings should be cleaned, all the lights and beams
 should be washed down.

 All cleaning should be done well in advance wherever possible. To clean pits and lines, 90 bbl of
 water containing 1 to 2 drums of CLEAN SURF (as contingency) should be mixed up and circulated
 through all lines, gun lines, mixing lines etc. This can also be used to clean the tank system initially.

       Pump should be worked at the maximum safe rate.
       The below check list should be filled by the supervisor in the site.

            Equipment                     Complete

              Brine Storage Tanks

              Transfer Lines

                  Pill and Slug Pits

              Reserve/Mix Pit

             Rig Pumps

              Trip Tank

          Pump Charge Lines

            Cement Unit Lines

            Choke Unit Lines

                 Kill Lines

                           Drilling Program
                        Well : AZNS-118 (G04)
                           Type : IGH

             Page 114 of 177               Doc. No.: AZD6-EN-WP-020-1                     Rev: 1

        It should be noted that all dump valves should seal with grease to ensure they are in good order.

       All ditch gates should be sealed with silicon on each side of the gate.  This will need to be
     replaced if the gate is opened.

      UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES SHOULD BARITE, BENTONITE OR POLYMERS BE USED
   TO SEAL ANYTHING.

       All pump packing should be examined before starting the cleaning.

G.6.2.    Displacement Design
 To ensure effective mud displacement and water wetting of the casing, the displacement pill needs to be
 designed carefully. The use of a weighted push pills with a viscosity greater than that of the mud, will
 minimize channeling and ensure good cleaning of the low side of the well bore.

 The best fluid for thinning the mud is the continuous phase of the mud. In addition, SPERSEEN CFL
 could be used to reduce the yield point and gel strengths. The yield point should be between 8 to10 Pa
 and the 10 minute gel to <10 Pa. The actual quantity of material required to do this must be determined
 by the pilot testing performed by the mud engineer to determine the most cost-effective treatment.

 Throughout the drilling fluid conditioning process, the flow rate used should be the maximum practical
 rate.

       The drill string should be reciprocated and rotated during the operation. The combined effect of
       scrapers being run in the hole, the high flow rate and the reciprocation/rotation will help to
      remove/disperse large quantities of mud solids and general debris. The reciprocation stroke
      should be +/- 10 m. and the rotation speed should be +/- 60 RPM

       During this operation, as much of the surface volume of mud as possible should be removed from
       the pits to accommodate the inhibited water and the well clean up pills. Once the mud has been
       back-loaded, surface preparation can be done.

       At least 150 m of pill/spacer coverage or 3 min contact time at the highest pump rates should be
       considered.

       Pit levels should be monitor throughout the displacement operation to catch and prevent an influx
       entering the well contributing to an incident.

G.6.3.    Completion Fluids Design and Formulation

 Completion Fluid Formulation and Mixing Procedure

     Completion Fluid : Inhibited Calcium Chloride Brine (80 pcf)

                                                                                 Concentration
               Additives             Material Description         Function
                                                                                                  (lb/bbl)      Gal/bbl

               Water                      Water                Base Fluid          273.4        33

      CALCIUM CHLORIDE DH           CaCl2                Weighting Agent       173.08             -

               LIME                 pH Control             pH Control           0.5-1              -

           BRINE-COR                Corrosion Inhibitor          Corrosion Inhibitor         3.5          0.4

          H2S SCAV P            H2S Scavenger         H2S Scavenger          1.8                -

            BIO-CIDE HP                    Biocide                     Biocide             0.4         0.04

          OX SCAV P             Oxygen Scavenger        Oxygen Scavenger        1.1                -

         1.  Fill the tanks with the required volume of Drill water.
         2. Add ±173.08 lb/bbl CaCl2 to the Drill water tank to get 80 pcf brine. (Mud Weight should
          be monitored while adding CaCl2)
         3. Add ± 0.5-1 lb/bbl of Lime for maintaining alkalinity.
         4. Add 3.5 lb/bbl (0.4 gal/bbl) of BRINE-CORE (Corrosion inhibitor)
         5. Add ± 1.8 lb/bbl of H2S SCAV P
         6. Add 0.4 lb/bbl (0.04 gal/bbl) of BIO-CIDE.
         7. Add ± 1.1 lb/bbl of OX SCAV P (to eliminate dissolved oxygen as a source of corrosion)

 Note1: OX SCAV P addition should be done at the last stage just before Brine displacement in the
 hole. It should be mixed slowly to reduce the amount of air entrained in the brine and the amount of
 oxygen which may be incorporated into the system, also use of the mixing hopper and agitation of
 the completion fluid by surface equipment should be minimized.

Preparation before Cementing Job
   1)  Equipment inspection and maintenance.

   2)  Pump rate and other instrument calibration.

   3)  Water and dry cement preparation.

   4)  Cement additive preparation.

   5)   Pilot lab test with different ratio of drilling fluid and cement slurry using rig water.

   6)  High pressure lines and manifold connection with standby lines.

   7)  Submission of cementing program 24 hrs before cementing operation.

   8)  Pre-job meeting with all involved personnel and issuing the job procedure.

   9)  Double check all preparation jobs by every position.

   10) Perform Pilot test on cement slurry, take sample from cement solution for testing.

   11) Check wiper plug in LDC for Leakage. Check ball size in LDC.

   12) Perform Function test, flow through & hold test for float shoe & float collar in start of running

         Liner.

Drilling waste management plan shall be developed and implemented, and appropriate actions shall
be taken to prevent environmental pollution, conserve resources and minimize waste. CONTRACTOR
shall continually strive to minimize the impact of their WORK on the environment. Plans shall be
enveloped where elimination of a pollution source is not practical, appropriate treatment of waste shall
be undertaken and monitored to minimize the impact of discharges and disposals on the environment.
The waste treatment and disposal shall be performed during the Drilling period. The system should
consist of following separation, containment and handling equipment, and treatment and disposal.

1. Separation equipment: high efficiency solid and liquid separation system as described in
Schedule IV.

2. Containment and handling equipment:
 Conveyer: for collection and discharge of all cuttings.
 drying shale shaker: giving dryer cuttings and reduced mud consumption.
 Contingency tanks: Arrangement for the occasional collection, separation and isolation of cutting
wastes.
 Fluid sump: for the collection of site drains and excess drilling fluid.
 Tanks: for the storage of excess fluid prior of treatment.
 Pumps: for transfer fluids.
 Backhoe, dump truck, etc. for the transportation of disposals
3. Treatment and disposal:
 Fixation: using cement or similar to stabilize the salt or chemicals.
 dewatering of excess fluids, site water, and water based drilling fluid.
Disposal area will be designated by COMPANY and CONTRACTOR shall transfer fixed cuttings to this
location at CONTRACTOR‟s cost.
CONTRACTOR shall refer to the following standards for the effluent limits.

Treatment and Disposal Systems.

      Drilling fluids
      Drilling Cuttings

    Dewatering Process Advantages
    60% to 85% Recovery of the aqueous phases from the waste mud
     40% reduction of waste volume and transportation.
     The water phase contained into the waste volume is almost totally recovered and re-
       sent back to the rig for new mud mixing, rig activities etc. This will drastically reduce
       the cost of transportation for the water needed for operations.
      Reduction in waste pit size and smallest foot print
      Produced water should be tested for different ions.
     Dispose water from rig site shall be clear, Ca<800 mg/lit, 7<PH<8

     Cutting Transfer System
Cuttings transfer system is required to collect all the solids discharge from solids control
equipment. This system is installed under Shale Shaker and Centrifuge Area.

     Cutting Treatment Process
Cuttings treatment is important part of the waste management services which is usually done to
solidification and stabilize and fix the liquid phase movement on the solids.

Solidification refers to techniques that encapsulate the waste in a monolithic solid of high
structural integrity. In this treatment, material is added to reduce free water and possibly reduce
or slow potential contaminant release. Contaminant migration is restricted by vastly decreasing
the surface area exposed to leaching by isolating the wastes within an impervious capsule.
Stabilization refers to those techniques that reduce the hazard potential of wastes by converting
contaminants into their least soluble, mobile, or toxic form. The physical nature and handling
characteristics of the waste are not necessarily changed by stabilization.

1.1   COMPANY is committed to conducting operations in a manner which minimizes the risks to the
        health and safety of those involved in, and affected by, such operations. COMPANY is also
       committed to conducting its operations in a manner which minimizes the impact on natural and
           ‘built’ environments in the area of operations.

1.2     This section sets out minimum Quality, Health, Safety and Environmental (QHSE) requirements
         for the WORK that CONTRACTOR and subcontractors will be required to comply with whilst
       conducting operations for COMPANY.

1.3   COMPANY may perform audits and assessments of CONTRACTOR’s and its subcontractors’
       performance under the CONTRACT. COMPANY reserves the right without prior notice to
       conduct quality, health, safety, security and environmental audits of the Operations.

1.4   CONTRACTOR shall at all times be responsible for performing the WORK in a manner so as to
        protect against loss of life, injury to people, damage to property and the environment. The
        detailed manner means and methods of performing the WORK shall be under the control and
         direction of CONTRACTOR.

1.5     Prior to the start of Operations, certain QHSE processes must be completed. These QHSE
       processes include developing the final QHSE plan format and frequency of any QHSE audits,
        permitting and  licensing and COMPANY’s approvals. CONTRACTOR  shall ensure  that
         sufficient resources are dedicated to this task to ensure completion prior to mobilization.

1.6   COMPANY may at any time stop the WORK or any portion of the WORK without penalty to
     COMPANY  if the WORK is not conducted in accordance with the Quality, Health, Safety or
       Environmental guidelines specified in this CONTRACT or by the laws of the appropriate
         jurisdiction. COMPANY reserves the right to require CONTRACTOR to remove any person from
        the Operations in the case of non-compliance with QHSE procedures. COMPANY may also
         prohibit the use of equipment and plant in cases where that equipment or plant does not meet
        the required standards or is deemed unsafe.
1.7   CONTRACTOR shall ensure that activities associated with this CONTRACT are conducted in
       compliance with applicable national and local HSE laws and regulations, CONTRACTOR’s
       standards and COMPANY’s requirements and IADC documents.
1.8     Limits of Authority

      COMPANY’s Representative(s) do not have the authority to relax health, safety or environment
        standards. If they judge the Operation to be inadequate with regards to any aspect of quality,
        health, safety, security or the environment, then the operation may be immediately suspended.

1.9   QHSE Plan

     CONTRACTOR shall be required to develop a project-specific QHSE plan to manage the
     WORK and associated risks. This plan shall, as a minimum, address topics included in the list
        detailed in Item 7. Where existing CONTRACTOR QHSE publications detail the topics listed, it
          is sufficient to either include them verbatim, or provide reference to where they may be found in
      CONTRACTOR’s QHSE  Manuals. The  final  project-specific QHSE  plan  shall  satisfy
     CONTRACTOR standards, COMPANY requirements and applicable HSE laws and regulations.

1.10   Contractor should establish an effective HSE system and implement it strictly.

1.11    Contractor must adhere to the standards and regulations of Health, Safe and Environment
        constituted by the local government.

     COMPANY  to  verify  an  appropriate  program  of  immunizations  consistent  with  the

        Well Control        Well Control

(1)  Recording Reference

All BOP tests, drills, function tests, any malfunctions, repair or maintenance to the mud system and
well control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the
Drilling Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded
in the Daily Drilling Report.

(2)  Flow Check Procedure

To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during
the drilling operation.

     1)  While drilling(any warning sign)

     2)   Prior to tripping the drill string

     3)  While tripping(any warning sign)

     4)  While out of hole(continuously)

     5)   Trip out:

        After pulling 5% of the drill pipe
        At the midpoint depth of the wellbore
        Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars
        After all the drill string is out of hole.

     6)   Trip in:

       Upon reaching surface casing shoe
        At midpoint of the wellbore

(3)  Primary Control Reference

It is the responsibility of the Drilling Contractor to keep the hole full at all times by using all the
available equipment. The Drilling Supervisor shall monitor that the correct preventive practices are
being implemented and/or conducted at all times.

Extreme care shall be taken to monitor mud volume, drilling breaks and gas cut mud.

The MACP (Maximum allowable casing pressure) shall be confirmed by the Drilling Supervisor, either
after setting each new casing string or, whenever the density of the drilling mud changes.

The MACP shall be clearly written on a kick control sheet that will be posted near the choke control
panel.
 Health, Safety and Environment                                      Page 156 of 177
 Development Well

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                        Drilling Program
                     Well : AZNS-118 (G04)
                        Type : IGH

         Page 157 of 177               Doc. No.: AZD6-EN-WP-020-1                     Rev:1

The predetermined distance at which the Tool Joint is to be pulled above the rotary should be posted
on rig floor near the BOP control panel.

The Driller is responsible for carefully measuring and recording the slow pump pressure. Awareness of
these values is an important element in killing operations, in order to avoid formation breakdown.

Take a measure and record the slow pump pressure at three different flow rates with all pumps at the
following times:

       Once per tour.
       Whenever changes occur in the mud density/rheology.
       Whenever changes occur in the dimension and characteristics of the string , BHA, jet
                size, jet plugged or jet lost, etc.

(4)  Secondary Control Reference

Any time a drilling break is noticed, drilling shall stop and a static monitoring of the well shall be carried
out. Space-out for all Pipe Rams and Annular Preventer must be known to the Driller at all times to
keep tool joints clear of Annular preventer and rams.

(5)  Kick Detection Procedure While Drilling

If there is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the Driller shall follow the kick detection
procedures outlined below:

Stop drilling with the pump onPick up top drive to a predetermined space-out positionShut off the
pumps and check for well flow by visual examination on the bell nipple or flow line.

     1)    If the well is not flowing:

        Immediately notify the rig manager, Drilling Supervisor and Toolpusher.
       The Drilling Supervisor will decide whether to circulate bottoms up or resume drilling. The
              penetration rate  will be limited as long as the cause of the abnormal situation  is
             undetermined. Always be aware that some hydrocarbons (gas or oil cut mud) may rise to
              the surface. Ensure that the proper monitoring and safety systems all in place.

     2)    If the well is flowing:

        Close the well as per the Shut-in Procedure.
      Immediately notify the Wellsite Drilling Supervisor, rig manager and Toolpusher.

          H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure         H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure
9.1     Monitoring H2S

      1) Somewhere on the well site is apt to accumulate H2S, such as mud pit, shale shaker, and
            drilling platform, should be installed one set of. Make sure H2S monitor and alarm system
        can be used.

      2) Alarm threshold setting for H2S warning indicator: the first warning level is 10mg/m3, unable
         warning sound, just show present value of H2S content to operators. The second warning
          level is 20mg/m3, when the H2S content in air exceed 20mg/m3, H2S warning indicator can
         give an alarm automatically, and warning sound should be heard by everyone work in well
            site. The audible alarm should be installed on Kelly board.

      3) Equip enough gas masks on drilling platform, shaker screen (total amount should large than
          24), and equip 12 sets of 30min positive pressure Air Aspirators，2 sets of portable H2S
         monitor and appropriative H2S warning indicator. Arrange a person specially assigned for
          taking charge all the protective apparatus. This man must do periodical check to keep these
        equipment in a good condition.

 Health, Safety and Environment                                      Page 157 of 177
 Development Well

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                        Drilling Program
                     Well : AZNS-118 (G04)
                        Type : IGH

         Page 158 of 177               Doc. No.: AZD6-EN-WP-020-1                     Rev:1

      4) H2S monitor should be done weekly check and compulsory examination.

      5) After drilling into the pay zone, strengthen the detection of H2S content in mud.

      6) Contractor shall implement H2S service system by himself or 3rd party for controlling the risk
          of H2S leakage.

9.2    Measures for H2S prevention

      1) Windsocks shall be set on the drill floor and in the monsoon direction or/and prevailing wind
          direction of Azadegan  oil  field,  off well site. In emergency, employees must follow the
         evacuation procedure.

      2) Explosion-proof blowers shall be installed around the rig, shale shaker, and drilling fluid tanks
          to blow away toxic and flammable gas at the well site.

      3) The rig crew in the H2S area shall be furnished with H2S monitors and adequate protective
         apparatus in accordance with IPS. Everybody shall be able to use, maintain, and check the
         apparatus.

      4) The technicians of rig crew are responsible for H2S proof training and the tool pusher is in
        charge of the supervision and examination.

      5) The pH value of drilling fluid in the H2S area shall be kept over 9.5. Pay attention to
        measurement of H2S concentration in drilling fluid. The H2S concentration shall be kept at
          less than 50mg/cm3 by using sulphur removal agents and degassers.

      6) Personnel safety and protection shall be carried out according to IPS during operations in
          polluted areas where H2S content exceeds the critical concentration.

      7) When the rig crew makes decision to bleed and fire because well control cannot be performed
        due to well site conditions, operations shall be performed according to procedures in IPS.

      8) Once blowout occurs, the incident shall be reported to the higher level department as soon as
         possible and fire fighting trucks, ambulances, medical care personnel and technicians shall be
        on duty at the well site.

      9) After the blowout is controlled, H2S concentration should be measured in the places where
       H2S is possible to gather.

      10) The personnel are not allowed to access until the H2S concentration is below the critical
          concentration.

CONTRACT shall provide the H2S monitoring and control services (EQUIPMENT and personnel) to protect
against high concentrations of H2S gas expected through the DRILLING OPERATION, details includes without
limitation:

(1)    to ensure all H2S equipment is in good condition,

(2)    to supply, maintain, inspect, calibrate and repair all H2S equipment to the highest standard and have this
      equipment ready for use all the time,

(3)    to supply the gas detectors & required accessories to automate the gas detection program with capabilities
       of continually evaluate the condition of the gas monitor and should be able to collect information and
      provide automate & manual alerts regarding the status of the available toxics gases,

(4)    to review COMPANY’s H2S evacuation procedure and to advise where change/modifications are required,

(5)    to monitor levels of H2S, inform COMPANY, and take any necessary precautions to safeguard life, the
       well and the Equipment from impending danger,

(6)    to customise safety training program,

(7)    to maintain a minimum inventory of parts and accessories to facilitate ease and quality provision of service,

(8)    to prepare and submit detailed technical and quality reports on timely basis.

(9)   To keep to be available at rig site on 24 hours/day.

(10)  The supply of different types (fixed multi-sensor, portable, and electronic, and non-electronic, sampling
       type) of H2S gas detection equipment to be installed, tested and commissioned on the rig that will perform
       the drilling, complete with dual level (10-20ppm) visual and audible alarms at different points of the rig
         site, to allow for early warning of all personnel on the rig for H2S gas occurrence in the atmosphere, hence
       ease of following emergency plans to safety briefing areas. All equipment and devices shall be on location
       before well SPUND-IN, service personnel shall be on location before spud in the hole section which contain
     H2S or other poisonous gases.

(11)  The supply of a comprehensive cascade breathing air loop system, complete with breathing air supply
      compressors, storage cylinders, and work/escape and rescue breathing apparatus. This system shall provide
        at time of gas detection and alarm for essential personnel, who will be responsible to control the well during
       emergencies, an extended period of time under fresh breathing air, to allow for non-essential personnel to
      escape to safe briefing areas, and for rescue teams to rescue any injured persons during H2S emergencies.

(12)  The safety supervision performed by qualified personnel at rig site, to install, commission and maintains in
      good condition the H2S safety equipment, to train rig personnel, COMPANY and Third Party personnel on
     H2S emergency procedures and use of the H2S safety equipment and to assist in carrying out the H2S
       Safety Plan.

COMPANY’s requirements are noted below.
